channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest Brussels posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: Fire that damaged cars in Saint-Gilles was a case of arson, say police
item.description: According to local police, one car was deliberately set alight and the fire then spread to a second vehicle parked nearby.

item.title: Brussels extends drug 'hotspot' strategy despite doubts over efficacy
item.description: Brussels is extending its drug hotspots despite the lack of an overall assessment of their effectiveness.

item.title: Firefighter who died in Brussels gas explosion to receive state funeral
item.description: Olivier Francotte, the firefighter who died during the gas explosion last Friday near Brussels Central Station, will receive a state funeral.

item.title: Brussels says it is prepared to deal with fire risk in the Sonian Forest
item.description: A fire in the Sonian Forest could pose a major risk because of the drought, the number of visitors it attracts, and its proximity to the capital.

item.title: Two cars on fire in broad daylight in Saint-Gilles
item.description: Emergency services were called to Rue Vanderschrick at around 16:00 on Tuesday, where they found two cars on fire. A third vehicle was also damaged.

item.title: 'Irresponsible': Brussels protest denounces plan to scrap 1,000 shelter spaces
item.description: The Federal Migration Minister said she recognised that "migration has a significant impact on Brussels" but that the issue is "very complex".

item.title: 'Make Humanity Shine': Why you shouldn't skip this new exhibition in Brussels
item.description: If you've passed through the city centre of Brussels in the last few days, you may have noticed a series of portraits and panels – here's why they're worth reading.

item.title: Greening of Brussels EU quarter starts with redevelopment of historic street
item.description: "We are doing away with a layout that is currently dominated by tarmac and car parks."

item.title: New Brussels festival to shine a spotlight on emerging artists
item.description: Described as a “festival of the rejected”, the event aims to boost visibility for up-and-coming artists working in film, music, painting and stand-up comedy.

item.title: Cameroonian rapper found guilty of sexual assaults in Bois de la Cambre
item.description: The man reportedly assaulted his victims from behind while threatening them with a knife when they were leaving a nightclub.

item.title: Brussels PS leader files complaint over racism and death threats
item.description: The socialist said a police investigation was launched after he reported racist remarks and death threats made against him to the authorities.

item.title: Brussels police arrest minor with drugs and a stolen scooter
item.description: An officer spotted the suspect riding a scooter on the pavement in the centre of Brussels and stopped him for a check.

item.title: Code yellow drought alert in Brussels despite forecast rain
item.description: Authorities have put measures in place and are urging people to use mains water responsibly.

item.title: Brussels doctor writes to Federal Government about 'long-term impact' of aircraft noise
item.description: "As a doctor, I am seriously concerned about the impact of long-term aircraft noise on residents."

item.title: City of Brussels to compensate owner-occupiers for higher property tax
item.description: Homeowners in the City of Brussels will receive their property tax assessment notices in the coming days.

item.title: Eurostar struggles with overcrowding as London terminal remains unchanged
item.description: Some 45,000 passengers pass through Eurostar's cramped London terminal every day, with numbers expected to rise in the coming years. How will the station accommodate them all?

item.title: Brussels canal in a poor state with pollution, green algae and dead fish
item.description: Brussels Environment confirmed the presence of green algae and said it would send a team to the site as soon as possible to examine the situation.

item.title: Violent car theft suspect detained after motorway police chase
item.description: Officers tried to force the car to slow down, but the driver allegedly refused to stop. Prosecutors said the suspect also tried to ram police vehicles.

item.title: Several planes harassed by lasers when landing at Brussels Airport
item.description: Shining lasers at aircraft can blind or disorientate pilots during landing. It is therefore illegal in Belgium.

item.title: Brussels Airlines launches new flights to meet demand for Arctic holidays
item.description: Brussels Airlines said winter trips to the polar region are becoming increasingly popular.
